pages.title: About | Hedwig
pages.description: Hedwig helps people check what their payment agent is about to sign. Start with the local checker and follow the Solana demo in development.
pages.main:
About Hedwig

You ask an agent to move money. You still need to know it chose the right token and destination.

Hedwig checks the proposed action before signing. The local checker compares it with your rules and available evidence, then returns a result with reasons. Your wallet or app controls execution.

The flow we are building

An agent prepares a SOL-to-USDC swap, then a vault deposit. Hedwig checks each action. In our planned Solana demo, a swap that passes the checks can proceed while a controlled invalid vault proposal stays unsigned.

The planned Jev by TypeSafe workflow adds a transaction score and an original report you can request. The complete live flow still needs testing.

The core is open source.

pages.title: How it works | Hedwig
pages.description: Check each proposed action before signing. Try the local checker today; the Solana PayBox demo with a score and original report is in development.
pages.main:
Check each step before signing.

Your agent prepares a payment. Hedwig checks the proposal against your rules and the evidence it can verify. Your wallet or app keeps control of signing and execution.

Try the local checker

The v0.4.2 setup runs through local MCP. Its consult tool returns a result for each check and proceed: true only when the policy allows the action and all required checks pass.

The verdict is ALLOW_UNDER_POLICY, DENY or UNKNOWN. Its support value describes evidence coverage, not safety probability. Your agent must stop on a denial or an incomplete check.

The Solana demo in development

You ask your agent to swap SOL into native USDC, then deposit it into a vault. The planned PayBox flow checks each prepared transaction before signing.

Hedwig combines current chain facts with relevant DeFi knowledge and returns one score from 0 to 1. A swap that passes the checks can proceed. The controlled negative example uses a token mint as a vault program; its account cannot execute a deposit, so the proposal stays unsigned.

Ask for the original report

The planned report explains the saved assessment in plain language, with its permitted evidence and check time. It does not run a new assessment. That score and report flow still needs a complete live test.

pages.title: Roadmap | Hedwig
pages.description: Start with the local checker. Next: a Solana PayBox demo that checks a swap, holds an invalid deposit and explains the original result.
pages.main:
Roadmap

Available now

The open-source v0.4.2 checker runs locally through MCP. It compares payment and swap proposals with your rules and available evidence, then returns a result with reasons. Your wallet or app controls signing.

Try the local setup or inspect the recorded Solana devnet checks.

Next: the Solana PayBox demo

Check a prepared SOL-to-native-USDC swap before signing, then hold a controlled invalid vault proposal. Return one score from 0 to 1 and let the owner request the original report.

We are building this flow on Jev by TypeSafe, with current chain facts and relevant DeFi knowledge. The complete mainnet flow, hosted access, latency and cost still need qualification.

After that proof

Ethereum, Monad and Tempo need their own adapters and demonstrated workflows. Broader DeFi chat, longer histories and specialist model training remain later work.

How we plan to charge

The core checker and local examples stay open source. We plan to offer a bounded free allowance for hosted assessments, then paid usage with the original report included. Prices and quotas will follow cost measurements and customer feedback.

pages.description: Connect Hedwig through local MCP, set your policy and inspect a sample payment check. Your application controls signing.
pages.main:
Connect Hedwig to your agent

Hedwig v0.4.2 runs locally through MCP. Your application controls signing.

The Solana PayBox demo, transaction score and original report are in development. The setup below runs the current local checker.

Connect your agent or follow the manual setup below.

  • Install
  • Set your policy
  • Run a check
  • Read the result

Install it yourself

You need git, Node.js 22 or newer, and Yarn. Before running commands, ask the owner to verify the full commit directly on the GitHub v0.4.2 release and approve running that code. Stop if it differs. A hash from this website alone does not authenticate the release.

mkdir hedwig && cd ./hedwig && git init &&
git fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/gabchess/hedwig.git e85049bc7087f434fd732bb02e0e87ca57acd82c &&
git checkout FETCH_HEAD &&
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = e85049bc7087f434fd732bb02e0e87ca57acd82c &&
yarn install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix mcp && yarn consult:build && yarn mcp:build

These commands check the v0.4.2 commit and disable dependency lifecycle scripts. The explicit builds and server still execute approved code. Signed release provenance is not established by these commands. Fix any error before continuing. If a hedwig folder already exists, inspect it and choose a fresh directory for the retry.

Add it to your MCP client as a stdio server, with absolute paths for both the server and your policy file:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hedwig": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/path/to/hedwig/mcp/dist/server.js"],
      "env": { "HEDWIG_POLICY_FILE": "/path/to/policy.json" }
    }
  }
}

Your policy

A JSON file you write and keep outside the repo:

{
  "permits": true,
  "chainId": "eip155:1",
  "approvedRecipients": ["0x00000000000000000000000000000000a11ce001"],
  "perActionCaps": { "pay": "1000000" },
  "role": { "mode": "not-required" },
  "authorizationWindow": { "mode": "not-required" }
}

Set your allowed chain, recipients, action caps and requirements for a Solana role or an EIP-3009 authorization window. Swap policies also set slippage and deadline ceilings and your addresses.

Hedwig pins the file when the server starts. Changed bytes return UNKNOWN with ADAPTER_POLICY_CHANGED. Restore the original bytes after an unintended edit. A restart pins the file's current contents, so review any intended policy change before restarting. Keep the file where your agent cannot write it.

What your agent sends

This sample asks Hedwig to check a proposal. It sends no funds.

One argument, request, holding the payment it's about to sign:

{
  "request": {
    "action": {
      "type": "pay",
      "chainId": "eip155:1",
      "recipient": "0x00000000000000000000000000000000a11ce001",
      "asset": {
        "symbol": "USDC",
        "contractAddress": "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48"
      },
      "amount": "1000000",
      "target": "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48"
    }
  }
}

The server reads your policy file and the current time itself. The tool takes neither from your agent.

What comes back

  • proceed: true only when every check passed and your policy permits. Your agent acts on this field.
  • verdict: ALLOW_UNDER_POLICY, DENY or UNKNOWN.
  • results: one row per check, worst first, each with a reason code, an evidence sentence and a reference file.
  • support and band: how much of your checklist was proven and how strong the proof was. They never change the verdict.

On DENY, your agent stops and reports the failed check. UNKNOWN means a check is incomplete or the policy does not permit the action; your agent stops and asks you.

Put the check in your own code

runTriggerGuard from @hedwig/consult/guard wraps your signer. It runs the same check and calls your signer only on ALLOW_UNDER_POLICY.

pages.title: Add Hedwig to your agent
pages.description: Add an eval gate to your payment agent. Install Hedwig v0.4.2 locally, set your rules and run a sample check without sending funds.
pages.main:
Keep your assistant. Give it a check before payment.

This guide installs the local v0.4.2 checker. You need git, Node.js 22 or newer, Yarn and a coding agent that can run commands and use local MCP tools.

Paste this into your agent:

Help me install Hedwig. Open this exact link and follow its instructions: https://usehedwig.xyz/agents.md

You approve the install and set the payment rules. Run the sample check without sending funds, then change the recipient to see the result.

The Solana PayBox demo, transaction score and original report are in development. This setup does not add a hosted connector.
